newsitem.title: LEBANON: Lebanon issues money supply statistics.
newsitem.headline: Lebanon issues money supply statistics.

text.p: Lebanon's May M3 money supply grew a moderate 0.94 percent to 31,128 billion pounds, the Bank of Lebanon said on Friday.
"M3 growth was moderate during May. Its annual rate was 27.08 percent against 27.40 percent in April and 27.38 percent in March," the bank said in its latest monthly bulletin.
M1 money stock grew an annual 16.24 percent and declined 2.18 percent from April.
"Monetary growth in May was held down by the decline in net claims on the public sector and the appreciation of the Lebanese pound," the bank said.
M2 and M4 registered annual growths of 41.35 percent and 31.97 percent, respectively.
"M2 growth remains strong reflecting continuous shift towards the Lebanese pound. M2 represented 49.61 percent of total liquidity," the bank said.

The Bank defined the aggregates as follows:
M1 -- Currency in circulation + Demand deposits
M2 -- M1 + Other deposits in Lebanese pounds
M4 -- M3 + Treasury bills held by the non-banking system
